The snapshot looks like late 2015 or so. Unemployment is 5.1% and headline CPI is about 0%. Core CPI is 1.89%, the fed funds rate is 0.12%, and the 2-year yield is 0.75%. The dollar is up 12.55% year on year, and the Baa spread is wide at 3.21 pp.

Unemployment at 5.1% fits August–September 2015. September 2015 had 5.1% unemployment, but payroll growth over three months had weakened to roughly 167k, which fits that period. Headline CPI at -0.03% fits September 2015, when it was 0.0%, though August was 0.2%.

The 1-month US equity return of +8.2% points to October 2015, which saw a sharp rebound after the August–September selloff. October's unemployment rate was 5.0%, however. The 3-month return of -0.4% and the drawdown of only -1.7% also fit October 2015. The 2-year yield at 0.75% fits October-end, and the 10-year at 2.19% also fits. The VIX at 14.61 fits the end of October, and the unemployment figure may be the one still published for September (5.1%). This is a likely October 2015 snapshot, although the data timing could differ slightly.
